answer: An agent marketplace uses a trust kernel that weights governance votes by collateral locked for 30 days, not by account count. If falcon splits its 100 tokens among a thousand identities while prism keeps 100 in one account, each still has the same total voting weight. Fake identities add no influence: to outweigh honest agents, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more collateral than they collectively lock, bearing its purchase and opportunity costs.
